result.markdown:
For a small business in Australia, my recommendation would be **Xero** as the best all-round accounting software.

However, the best choice depends on whether you're a sole trader, run a small company, have employees, or manage stock.

Here are the options I'd shortlist for 2026.

## Best accounting software compared

![Small business, big stress – and finding the right balance for success](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/js_DP_ZcJt2b0HYevLiH8RyWaqBcysH-7umi2-OpUv1L_c7R6GqF2ePsaUUNhFEx0xoCJM9UhE2ygbfJvKTZATLo4fmY2I8PpXkEP4z5gNTNS9QARFCTPWNcGDYwVCjusvLzfwG5BpY7OHDvJf-Gvvkz7eUnU1rkY8PEcDFGKBEcxvEb1v6GA_F2cLDI9Uk_?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Xero**

(Best overall)

- Excellent bank reconciliation and invoicing.
- GST, BAS and payroll functionality.
- Strong integrations with Australian banks and business apps.
- Good for businesses that plan to grow.

Australian plans from approximately A\$37/month.

[Xero website](https://www.xero.com/au/)

---



**2\. MYOB**

(Best Australian alternative)

- Excellent Australian tax and payroll features.
- Good for businesses with employees.
- BAS and GST functionality.
- Particularly worth comparing if payroll is important.

Business plans from approximately A\$35/month.

[MYOB website](https://www.myob.com/au)

---

![Quickbooks Logo Png | Quickbooks Logo Vector  - freepng](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/EgpRGTuKXM9JBQhBxDeBmotPOK2V1CAxW6csrlBGPGPM15pztH3eOcpEVWcqc6mS0O1OJQxiy3rYDKVoibK-tXZzwx_-fnc0UCKsZf5bUQtlgBDTtK7dsXwaLO2yAIKNfloGWbyBHt0g2gG5iJtWLQko_1xFOodwaVRw5Zh1K1GZ7uleuWwINKnPwp3V07V7?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. QuickBooks**

- Good invoicing and expense management.
- Useful reporting and automation.
- Lots of integrations.
- Worth considering if your accountant already uses it.

Australian plans vary by subscription.

[QuickBooks website](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/au/)

---

!["Best 10 Zoho Apps for Small Businesses in 2024 - Must-Have Tools" | C3 Solutions](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/QMBJut4kUVy6UNtA0DcEcpSKElNdEgHfabBOoR3AWTMUo6phHjAJ01KBTRk_iU44CUuVy6AD0OeM48UFtluYC3mtudqFVjYFesk47WQPcQQfsgxz1-Ctp0z-lODm5vgYFvDQ7IEjwcEwqAsNX1booH4Twqog2tqxnwaLYmRuRR9TviU8hG6khxNJKfVoO6Q2?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Zoho Books**

- Good value for smaller businesses.
- Automation and recurring invoices.
- Integrates with other Zoho business products.
- Worth considering if keeping costs down is important.

[Zoho Books website](https://www.zoho.com/au/books/)

---

![Reckon Payroll 2026 Pricing, Features, Reviews & Alternatives | GetApp](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ACef1V9QbM8Y3LxjLzJIQV-TfChUBjwyyx7W6AOhVMywuWusbhYulcZYBn3S8A-J1ZSIIaQtu8WMi3CVnQm3fE7mKMbBw3Beo_sQTtWxx5CDDP34nqzqL6m70W1jmud24Hdj0BDI4_JPvo8A-h8b5n6w-92zDw-PxjtUuoZZ2u15XApkZg7xxx4sYiZVnXkz?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Reckon One**

- Affordable Australian accounting option.
- GST and bookkeeping functionality.
- Worth considering for businesses with simpler requirements.

[Reckon website](https://www.reckon.com/au/)

These recommendations reflect Australian small-business requirements, rather than US accounting software rankings. ## Which one should you choose?

| Your business situation | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| Small business with plans to grow | Xero |
| Sole trader | Xero or MYOB |
| Business with employees | Xero or MYOB |
| Service business / consulting | Xero |
| Retail or stock management | MYOB AccountRight or Xero with inventory integration |
| Tight budget | Zoho Books or Reckon |


## What I'd look for before buying

Make sure the software can\:

- Automatically import transactions from your bank.
- Reconcile income and expenses.
- Create professional invoices and quotes.
- Track GST and prepare BAS.
- Produce profit and loss reports.
- Manage payroll and superannuation if you employ staff.
- Share access with your accountant or bookkeeper.

One important tip: ask your accountant which software they prefer. Having them work directly in your accounting system can save considerable time and money.

search_results.description: The article compares small-business accounting software for 2026, emphasizing that the right platform can centralize bookkeeping, expenses, reporting, and tax tasks, while integrating with other business tools. Its top paid options include Rippling Spend for centralized expense management and workflow automation; Xero for broad features, reporting, and integrations, though its entry plan has strict limits; QuickBooks for its extensive product range and comprehensive tools; Sage Accounting for multi-user support and clear pricing; Zoho Books for automation and a free tier with revenue and user limits; Kashoo for straightforward use and multicurrency support; Wave for free accounting and invoicing, with paid support and payroll; and KashFlow for scalable, simplified online accounting. Free alternatives include ZipBooks, Money Manager Ex, GnuCash, VT Cash Book, and Adminsoft Accounts, each with different feature, platform, or support trade-offs. The article advises buyers to assess cost, scalability, reporting accuracy, support, integrations, and required features—especially payroll—before choosing. It distinguishes bookkeeping as recording daily transactions from accounting as compiling those records for financial statements and tax filing, and says its rankings reflect hands-on testing of usability, value, flexibility, and compatibility.
